questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following most accurately distinguishes mixed farming from mixed cropping?
options: Mixed farming is practised only in the rainforest zone while mixed cropping is practised only in the savanna
Mixed farming combines crop production with livestock rearing on the same farm, while mixed cropping grows two or more crops together
Mixed farming grows only cereals while mixed cropping grows only legumes
There is no real difference; the two terms mean exactly the same thing
questions.explanation: Mixed farming integrates crops and animals on one farm, whereas mixed cropping refers specifically to growing multiple crop species on the same piece of land simultaneously.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Shifting cultivation, as traditionally practised, primarily relies on which mechanism to restore soil fertility?
options: A fallow period during which natural vegetation regenerates and organic matter accumulates
Deep ploughing to bring subsoil nutrients to the surface
Continuous application of synthetic fertiliser every season
Irrigation with nutrient-rich river water
questions.explanation: Shifting cultivation abandons a plot after a few cropping seasons, allowing the bush to regrow and replenish soil nutrients before it is farmed again.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: A major disadvantage of monocropping compared with crop rotation or mixed cropping is that monocropping tends to
options: improve soil structure more than any other cropping system
deplete specific soil nutrients and encourage build-up of pests and diseases specific to that crop
automatically increase soil organic matter every season
eliminate the need for weed control entirely
questions.explanation: Growing the same crop repeatedly on the same land removes the same set of nutrients each season and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to persist and multiply.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Agroforestry is best defined as a land-use system in which
options: woody perennial trees or shrubs are deliberately combined with crops and/or livestock on the same land
crops are grown exclusively in greenhouses
only timber trees are planted for commercial logging
livestock are reared entirely indoors without access to pasture
questions.explanation: Agroforestry integrates trees with arable crops or animals, providing benefits such as shade, windbreaks, soil improvement, and additional income.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following is a primary role of the Federal Ministry of Agriculture in Nigeria's agricultural development?
options: Formulating national agricultural policy and coordinating programmes to boost food production
Manufacturing all farm machinery used in the country
Directly farming all land owned by private citizens
Setting the retail price of every food item sold in local markets
questions.explanation: Ministries of agriculture chiefly design policy, allocate resources, and coordinate national programmes rather than engage in direct farming themselves.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: A cooperative society benefits its farmer-members mainly by
options: eliminating the need for farmers to produce any crops themselves
guaranteeing that crop prices will never fall
replacing government extension services entirely
pooling resources to obtain inputs, credit, and better market access at lower individual cost
questions.explanation: Cooperatives allow members to combine bargaining power for inputs, credit, and produce sales, achieving economies of scale unavailable to individual smallholders.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which factor is most limiting to increased agricultural productivity among smallholder farmers in many parts of Nigeria?
options: Too much government subsidy on farm inputs
Overabundance of skilled agricultural labour
Excessive availability of arable land
Limited access to improved inputs, credit, and modern technology
questions.explanation: Smallholder productivity is commonly constrained by poor access to improved seeds, fertiliser, credit facilities, and mechanisation, keeping yields well below potential.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: The term 'plantation agriculture' refers to
options: large-scale cultivation of a single perennial cash crop, often for export
the rearing of poultry in battery cages
the practice of growing crops only in greenhouses
small plots of mixed food crops grown for household consumption
questions.explanation: Plantation agriculture involves extensive monoculture of crops such as oil palm, rubber, or cocoa, typically managed for commercial export rather than local subsistence.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of these best explains why agriculture is described as the backbone of many developing economies?
options: It employs a large proportion of the workforce and underpins food security, raw material supply, and export earnings
It requires no capital investment to operate successfully
It is the only sector that generates any government revenue
It has completely replaced industrialisation in most developing nations
questions.explanation: In many developing countries, agriculture remains the largest employer and a key source of food, industrial raw materials, and foreign exchange.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Sustainable agriculture is best described as farming practised in a manner that
options: maximises short-term yield regardless of long-term soil degradation
meets present food needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs
avoids any form of technology or mechanisation
relies solely on chemical inputs to guarantee output
questions.explanation: Sustainability balances current productivity with the conservation of soil, water, and biodiversity so that farming remains viable for future generations.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following is an example of an agro-allied industry that depends directly on agricultural raw materials?
options: A textile mill that processes cotton lint into fabric
A construction firm that builds residential apartments
A bank that offers only personal savings accounts
A telecommunications company providing mobile network services
questions.explanation: Agro-allied industries process farm produce; a textile mill using cotton lint as its raw material is a direct example of this linkage.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: A farm record showing the day-to-day income and expenditure of a farm business is best described as a
options: cropping calendar
weather forecast bulletin
soil survey map
cash account/financial record
questions.explanation: A financial record tracks money received and spent, enabling the farmer to assess profitability, unlike a soil map, calendar, or weather bulletin.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: An ecosystem is best defined as
options: a community of living organisms interacting with each other and their non-living environment
a man-made structure for storing farm produce
a single species of plant growing in isolation
the total land area used for crop production in a country
questions.explanation: An ecosystem encompasses both biotic (living) and abiotic (non-living) components and the interactions between them, such as a farm pond or a forest.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: In a farm food chain of grass to grasshopper to lizard to hawk, the hawk occupies which trophic level?
options: Primary consumer
Secondary consumer
Primary producer
Tertiary consumer
questions.explanation: Grass is the producer, the grasshopper is the primary consumer, the lizard is the secondary consumer, and the hawk, feeding on the lizard, is the tertiary consumer.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following best explains the ecological importance of decomposers such as bacteria and fungi in a farm ecosystem?
options: They convert atmospheric nitrogen directly into protein for animal consumption
They break down dead organic matter, releasing nutrients back into the soil for plant use
They prevent any form of soil erosion from occurring
They photosynthesise to produce food for the entire ecosystem
questions.explanation: Decomposers recycle nutrients locked in dead plant and animal matter, making them available again to producers and maintaining soil fertility.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Deforestation in the derived savanna zone of Nigeria has most directly contributed to
options: a decrease in the average daily temperature
a permanent increase in annual rainfall
an automatic improvement in soil fertility
increased soil erosion and gradual desertification-like degradation
questions.explanation: Removing tree cover exposes soil to wind and water erosion and reduces moisture retention, accelerating land degradation in fragile transitional ecological zones.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following is an abiotic component of a farm ecosystem?
options: Weeds
Soil pH
Crop pests
Earthworms
questions.explanation: Soil pH is a chemical/physical property of the environment (non-living), while earthworms, weeds, and pests are living (biotic) components.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Ecological succession on abandoned farmland typically begins with which group of colonising organisms?
options: Pioneer species such as grasses and other fast-growing herbaceous plants
Deep-rooted timber trees
Mature climax forest trees
Large grazing mammals
questions.explanation: Succession starts with hardy pioneer species that can colonise bare or disturbed soil, gradually being replaced by shrubs and eventually forest as conditions improve.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: The carrying capacity of a grazing land refers to
options: the number of years land can be left fallow
the total weight of farm machinery the soil can bear
the maximum number of livestock the land can support sustainably without degrading the pasture
the volume of water a dam can hold
questions.explanation: Carrying capacity is the stocking density a pasture can sustain long-term without overgrazing and subsequent degradation of the vegetation and soil.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Overgrazing in the savanna zone leads mainly to
options: an increase in soil organic matter content
a rise in pasture productivity over time
improved water infiltration into the soil
loss of vegetation cover, soil compaction, and increased erosion
questions.explanation: Excessive grazing removes protective vegetation faster than it can regrow, exposing and compacting the soil and making it more vulnerable to erosion.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which climatic factor most directly limits crop production in the Sahel ecological zone of Nigeria?
options: Excessively high relative humidity
Low and erratic rainfall
Very low sunlight intensity
Extremely acidic soil pH
questions.explanation: The Sahel zone's short, unreliable rainy season is the chief constraint on crop choice and productivity, favouring only drought-tolerant crops like millet and sorghum.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Symbiosis between rhizobium bacteria and leguminous plant roots is best classified as an example of
options: parasitism, since only the bacteria benefit
mutualism, since both organisms benefit from the association
commensalism, since only the plant benefits
predation, since the bacteria consume the plant
questions.explanation: Rhizobium bacteria fix atmospheric nitrogen for the plant's use, while the plant supplies the bacteria with carbohydrates, making it a mutually beneficial relationship.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the effect of wind as an ecological factor on crop production?
options: Wind only affects the colour of harvested produce
Wind has no measurable effect on any farming operation
Wind exclusively improves soil fertility
Strong winds can cause lodging of crops and increase the rate of transpiration and soil erosion
questions.explanation: High wind speeds can physically flatten tall crops (lodging), increase water loss through transpiration, and blow away loose topsoil.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following farm tools is most appropriate for shelling maize on a small scale?
options: A maize sheller
A wheelbarrow
A cutlass
A mould-board plough
questions.explanation: A maize sheller is specifically designed to separate maize grains from the cob, unlike a plough (tillage), cutlass (cutting/clearing), or wheelbarrow (transport).

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: A knapsack sprayer is a farm implement primarily used for
options: threshing cereal grains from their husks
applying liquid pesticides or herbicides to crops
measuring the moisture content of harvested grain
cutting down mature tree crops
questions.explanation: The knapsack sprayer, carried on the back, is designed to evenly distribute liquid agrochemicals such as pesticides or herbicides over a crop.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following farm structures is designed mainly to protect stored grain from moisture, pests, and rodents?
options: A grain silo/crib
A farrowing pen
An irrigation canal
A cattle crush
questions.explanation: Silos and cribs are storage structures engineered to keep grain dry, well-ventilated, and protected from pests and rodents after harvest.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: The main advantage of using a disc plough over a mould-board plough on land with many roots and stones is that the disc plough
options: leaves the soil completely unturned
cuts through roots and obstructions more easily due to its rotating discs
is used exclusively for spraying chemicals
requires no tractor power to operate
questions.explanation: The rotating discs of a disc plough slice through roots, stones, and tough sod more effectively than the fixed mould-board, making it suited to newly cleared or trashy land.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Planters (seed drills) are farm machines used mainly to
options: shell groundnuts after harvest
place seeds at a uniform depth and spacing during sowing
spray fungicide on standing crops
harvest root and tuber crops
questions.explanation: Seed drills/planters mechanise sowing, ensuring consistent seed depth and spacing, which improves germination uniformity compared with broadcasting by hand.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: A cutlass and hoe are classified together as
options: irrigation equipment
primary tillage machinery
processing machinery
simple hand tools
questions.explanation: Both the cutlass and hoe are manually operated implements without engines, distinguishing them from powered machinery or complex engineered structures.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which unit of a tractor is responsible for transmitting engine power to attached implements such as a mower or thresher?
options: The exhaust manifold
The steering wheel
The radiator
The power take-off (PTO) shaft
questions.explanation: The PTO shaft transfers rotational power from the tractor's engine to mounted or trailed implements, driving components such as a mower blade or thresher drum.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: A major safety precaution when operating a cutlass or any sharp farm tool is to
options: avoid wearing any protective clothing while working
leave the blade permanently blunt to avoid injury
operate it only at night
keep the blade sharp and always cut away from the body
questions.explanation: A sharp blade requires less force (reducing slip risk), and cutting motions directed away from the body minimise the chance of self-injury.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following best explains why farm machinery should be stored under a shed when not in use?
options: To protect it from rain, sun, and rust, thereby extending its useful life
To prevent it from being serviced regularly
To make it heavier for better traction
To increase its fuel consumption when next used
questions.explanation: Exposure to weather accelerates corrosion and material degradation; sheltered storage reduces rust and wear, prolonging the equipment's service life.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: An animal-drawn ridger differs from a tractor-mounted ridger mainly in its
options: basic function of forming ridges
requirement for a skilled operator
source of pulling power
use in crop production generally
questions.explanation: Both perform the same ridging function, but one is pulled by draught animals (e.g., oxen) while the other is powered and pulled by a tractor.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which soil separate has the smallest particle size and the greatest capacity to hold water and nutrients?
options: Sand
Silt
Gravel
Clay
questions.explanation: Clay particles are the smallest of the mineral soil separates, giving clay soils a large surface area that strongly retains water and nutrient ions.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Soil pH is a measure of the
options: amount of organic matter present in the soil
proportion of sand particles in the soil
depth of the water table below the soil surface
degree of acidity or alkalinity of the soil
questions.explanation: Soil pH quantifies hydrogen ion concentration, indicating whether a soil is acidic, neutral, or alkaline, which affects nutrient availability to plants.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Most arable crops grow best within a soil pH range of approximately
options: 9.0 to 10.0 (strongly alkaline)
2.0 to 3.0 (strongly acidic)
6.0 to 7.0 (slightly acidic to neutral)
0.0 to 1.0 (extremely acidic)
questions.explanation: Most nutrients are optimally available to plant roots within the slightly acidic to neutral pH range of about 6.0-7.0.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Liming an acidic soil is carried out primarily to
options: increase the sand content of the soil
lower the soil pH further
raise the soil pH and reduce aluminium and manganese toxicity
eliminate the need for any fertiliser application permanently
questions.explanation: Applying lime neutralises soil acidity, raising pH and reducing the solubility of toxic elements such as aluminium that harm plant roots in acidic soils.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following soil erosion control methods is most effective on steep hillsides used for farming?
options: Broadcasting seeds without any tillage
Terracing
Deep monocropping
Removing all vegetation cover
questions.explanation: Terracing breaks a slope into a series of level steps, slowing water runoff and reducing soil erosion on hilly or mountainous farmland.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Contour ploughing helps reduce soil erosion mainly by
options: creating furrows across the slope that slow down and trap surface water runoff
increasing the speed at which rainwater flows downhill
compacting the soil to prevent water infiltration entirely
removing organic matter from the topsoil
questions.explanation: Ploughing along the contour, rather than up and down a slope, creates ridges that intercept and slow runoff, reducing its erosive power.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Leaching in the soil refers to the process by which
options: organic matter is converted into humus
soluble nutrients are washed downward beyond the reach of plant roots by percolating water
soil particles are blown away by strong wind
nutrients are absorbed directly by plant roots
questions.explanation: Leaching moves dissolved nutrients down through the soil profile with water, often making them unavailable to shallow-rooted plants and contributing to soil infertility.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Soil fertility can be maintained or improved through all of the following practices EXCEPT
options: application of organic manure
practising a bush fallow period
continuous monocropping of the same nutrient-demanding crop every season
crop rotation with leguminous crops
questions.explanation: Continuous monocropping steadily depletes specific nutrients, whereas rotation, manuring, and fallowing all help restore or maintain soil fertility.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: The cation exchange capacity (CEC) of a soil is best described as its
options: ability to hold and exchange positively charged nutrient ions available to plants
capacity to transmit sound waves
resistance to compaction by farm machinery
total weight per unit volume
questions.explanation: CEC measures how many cations (e.g., calcium, potassium, magnesium) a soil can retain on its charged particle surfaces and later release to plant roots.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following soil organisms plays a major role in improving soil aeration and drainage through burrowing?
options: Earthworms
Soil-borne viruses
Nematodes that attack roots
Rust fungi
questions.explanation: Earthworms burrow through soil, creating channels that improve aeration and drainage while also mixing and enriching the soil with castings.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: A soil that drains poorly and remains waterlogged for long periods is most likely to have a high proportion of
options: coarse sand particles
well-decomposed humus only
clay particles
gravel
questions.explanation: Clay particles are so small and tightly packed that they leave very small pore spaces, restricting water movement and causing waterlogging in clay-dominated soils.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Green manuring involves
options: spraying green-coloured pesticide on crops
ploughing young, still-green leguminous or cover crops into the soil to improve fertility
painting farm structures green to reduce heat absorption
harvesting crops while they are still unripe
questions.explanation: Green manure crops are grown then incorporated into the soil while still green, adding organic matter and, if leguminous, fixing nitrogen.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Soil erosion caused by the removal of topsoil in thin, fairly uniform layers across a slope is known as
options: wind erosion
rill erosion
gully erosion
sheet erosion
questions.explanation: Sheet erosion removes a relatively even layer of topsoil across a broad area, often the earliest and least visible stage of water erosion, before it develops into rills or gullies.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Crop rotation is defined as the practice of
options: growing different crops in a planned sequence on the same piece of land over successive seasons
growing the same crop on the same land every season indefinitely
planting several unrelated crops randomly without any plan
rotating farm labourers between different farms
questions.explanation: Crop rotation deliberately alternates crops (often including a legume) across seasons to balance nutrient use, break pest cycles, and maintain soil fertility.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following is the most important reason for including a legume in a crop rotation cycle?
options: Legumes fix atmospheric nitrogen, enriching the soil for the crop that follows
Legumes require no water throughout their growth cycle
Legumes cannot be eaten by humans or animals
Legumes are immune to all pests and diseases
questions.explanation: Nitrogen-fixing legumes, through their root nodule bacteria, add usable nitrogen to the soil, benefiting the next crop in the rotation.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Seed dormancy refers to a condition in which
options: a viable seed fails to germinate even under favourable conditions until certain internal changes occur
a seed has completely lost its ability to germinate
a seed germinates immediately regardless of environmental conditions
a seed is destroyed by pests before planting
questions.explanation: Dormant seeds are alive and capable of germinating but are physiologically blocked from doing so until specific conditions (e.g., after-ripening) are met.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following is a recommended method of breaking hard seed-coat dormancy before planting?
options: Exposing the seed to direct sunlight for one hour only
Planting the seed immediately without any pre-treatment
Storing the seed at extremely low humidity indefinitely
Scarification of the seed coat
questions.explanation: Scarification physically or chemically weakens a hard seed coat, allowing water and oxygen to penetrate and trigger germination.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: The primary purpose of thinning young crop seedlings is to
options: increase the total number of plants per unit area indefinitely
eliminate the need for any weed control
prevent seeds from germinating at all
reduce competition for light, water, and nutrients among plants, allowing the remaining ones to grow better
questions.explanation: Thinning removes excess, weaker seedlings so the remaining plants have adequate space and resources, improving overall crop performance.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following weed control methods relies on the use of chemicals to kill unwanted plants?
options: Biological control using natural predators only
Chemical (herbicide) control
Mechanical control using a hoe
Cultural control through crop rotation
questions.explanation: Herbicides are chemical substances specifically formulated to kill or suppress weeds, distinct from mechanical, cultural, or biological weed control approaches.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: A pre-emergence herbicide is applied
options: only after the crop has fully matured and been harvested
exclusively to livestock feed
directly onto harvested grains in storage
to the soil before the crop and weed seeds germinate
questions.explanation: Pre-emergence herbicides form a chemical barrier in the soil that prevents germinating weed seeds from establishing, applied before seedlings emerge.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following pests is most commonly associated with causing significant damage to stored grains such as maize and cowpea?
options: Weevils
Mosquitoes
Tsetse flies
Ticks
questions.explanation: Weevils are notorious storage pests that bore into and feed on grains such as maize and cowpea, causing substantial post-harvest losses.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Crop rotation helps to reduce the incidence of soil-borne pests and diseases mainly because it
options: eliminates the need for any pest monitoring
increases the population of a single pest species over time
breaks the life cycle of pests and pathogens that depend on a specific host crop
provides a continuous host for pathogens every season
questions.explanation: Many pests and diseases are host-specific; rotating to a non-host crop deprives them of a suitable host, reducing their build-up in the soil.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the term 'monoculture'?
options: The cultivation of several different crops together on the same plot
The rearing of a single species of livestock alongside crops
The continuous cultivation of a single crop species on the same land over successive seasons
The practice of leaving farmland completely fallow every year
questions.explanation: Monoculture involves repeatedly growing one crop type on the same land, which can increase yield uniformity but heightens pest, disease, and soil-nutrient risks.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: The main purpose of mulching around growing crops is to
options: conserve soil moisture and suppress weed growth
reduce the organic matter content of the soil
prevent seed germination entirely
increase the rate of soil erosion
questions.explanation: A mulch layer (organic or plastic) reduces evaporation from the soil surface and blocks light needed by weed seedlings, conserving moisture and limiting weed competition.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which stage of crop production involves cutting and gathering mature crops from the field?
options: Nursery establishment
Transplanting
Land preparation
Harvesting
questions.explanation: Harvesting is the stage at which mature crops are cut, picked, or dug up from the field, following land preparation, planting, and crop husbandry stages.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Vegetative propagation of crops such as cassava and sugarcane is carried out using
options: spores
grafted root nodules from unrelated species
stem cuttings
true seeds only
questions.explanation: Cassava and sugarcane are typically propagated asexually using stem cuttings, which grow into new plants genetically identical to the parent.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following is an important reason for practising early planting at the onset of the rains in most parts of Nigeria?
options: It eliminates any need for subsequent weeding
It guarantees the complete absence of pests throughout the season
It allows crops to make maximum use of the available rainfall period for growth and maturity
It reduces the total yield obtainable from the crop
questions.explanation: Planting early ensures the crop's growth cycle aligns with the full length of the rainy season, maximising water availability for growth and yield.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of these is a cultural method of pest control?
options: Introducing a natural predator of the pest
Timely planting and proper crop rotation to avoid peak pest periods
Spraying a broad-spectrum synthetic insecticide
Applying a systemic fungicide
questions.explanation: Cultural pest control uses farming practices, such as adjusting planting dates or rotating crops, to reduce pest pressure without chemicals or introduced organisms.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following breeds of cattle is best known for high milk yield and is commonly kept for dairy purposes?
options: Friesian
N'Dama
Sokoto Gudali
White Fulani (Bunaji)
questions.explanation: The Friesian (Holstein-Friesian) breed is internationally renowned for its exceptionally high milk yield, making it a preferred dairy breed, often crossed with local breeds in the tropics.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Colostrum, the first milk produced by a mammal after giving birth, is important to the newborn mainly because it
options: is used only for making cheese
is harmful and should be withheld from the young
provides antibodies that boost the young animal's immunity against disease
contains no nutritional value at all
questions.explanation: Colostrum is rich in maternal antibodies that give newborn animals passive immunity during their first, most vulnerable days of life.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Culling in livestock management refers to the
options: castration of young male animals
removal of unproductive, diseased, or genetically undesirable animals from the herd
process of feeding animals a balanced ration
process of vaccinating all animals in a herd
questions.explanation: Culling improves overall herd quality and productivity by systematically removing animals that are unproductive, sick, or of poor genetic merit.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following poultry diseases is viral and highly contagious, often causing sudden high mortality in a flock?
options: Coccidiosis
Rickets
Fowl mites infestation
Newcastle disease
questions.explanation: Newcastle disease is a highly contagious viral disease of poultry that can spread rapidly and cause severe mortality if the flock is unvaccinated.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: A balanced livestock ration is one that
options: supplies all the nutrients an animal needs in the correct proportions for its stage of production
is given to the animal only once a week
consists of a single feed ingredient fed exclusively
contains only carbohydrates with no protein or minerals
questions.explanation: A balanced ration combines energy, protein, vitamins, and minerals in proportions appropriate to the animal's age, weight, and productive purpose (growth, milk, or egg production).

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Castration of young male livestock is carried out mainly to
options: increase the animal's fertility
reduce aggressiveness and improve meat quality by controlling unwanted breeding
eliminate the need for vaccination
prevent the animal from ever gaining weight
questions.explanation: Castrating males removes the testes, reducing aggressive behaviour and often improving carcass/meat quality while preventing indiscriminate breeding.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following is an important sign of a healthy farm animal?
options: Dull, sunken eyes with a rough coat and loss of appetite
Bright, alert eyes with a shiny coat and normal appetite
Persistent coughing and nasal discharge
Constant isolation from the rest of the herd or flock
questions.explanation: Healthy animals typically show alertness, a glossy coat, normal feeding behaviour, and active engagement with their environment, unlike sick animals which show the opposite signs.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: The deep litter system of poultry housing involves
options: raising birds entirely on wire mesh floors with no litter
confining each bird individually in a small wire cage
keeping birds exclusively in open free-range pasture with no housing
keeping birds on a floor covered with absorbent material such as wood shavings that is left to build up over time
questions.explanation: In deep litter housing, birds are raised on a floor covered with materials like wood shavings or rice husks, which absorbs droppings and is periodically turned rather than removed daily.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following is the main function of a brooder in poultry production?
options: To mix commercial feed for adult layers
To slaughter mature birds for sale
To store eggs before incubation
To provide artificial warmth and a controlled environment for day-old chicks
questions.explanation: Brooders supply the heat that day-old chicks need since they cannot yet regulate their own body temperature effectively, protecting them during the critical early weeks.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Artificial insemination in livestock breeding is mainly advantageous because it
options: allows genetically superior males to sire many offspring without natural mating and reduces disease transmission
eliminates the need for any record-keeping on the farm
guarantees that every offspring will be female
removes the need to feed breeding females
questions.explanation: AI enables semen from a single high-merit sire to inseminate many females, spreading superior genetics widely while reducing risks associated with natural mating, such as disease spread and injury.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which class of feed ingredient is maize primarily classified as in livestock nutrition?
options: A source of roughage only
A vitamin premix
An energy (carbohydrate) feed
A mineral supplement
questions.explanation: Maize is rich in starch/carbohydrate and is used mainly as an energy source in compounded livestock and poultry rations.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following is a common ectoparasite that infests the skin and feathers of poultry?
options: Fowl lice
Aflatoxin-producing mould
Coccidia
Newcastle virus
questions.explanation: Fowl lice live on the skin and feathers of birds (external/ectoparasites), unlike coccidia, viruses, and moulds which act internally or via toxins rather than as skin parasites.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Vaccination of livestock is carried out primarily to
options: improve the physical appearance of the animal's coat only
stimulate the animal's immune system to develop resistance against specific diseases
increase the animal's daily feed intake
cure an animal that is already showing severe symptoms of illness
questions.explanation: Vaccines are preventive, priming the immune system to recognise and fight a specific pathogen before natural infection occurs, rather than treating existing illness.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following best defines the term 'demand' in agricultural marketing?
options: The quantity of a commodity that consumers are willing and able to buy at a given price and time
The number of farmers who cultivate a particular crop
The amount of a commodity that spoils before it reaches the market
The total quantity of a commodity produced by all farmers in a season
questions.explanation: Demand in economics specifically refers to willingness and ability to purchase at a given price, not merely a desire or total production figures.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: According to the law of supply, as the price of an agricultural commodity rises, the quantity supplied by producers tends to
options: fall to zero immediately
remain completely unchanged regardless of price
decrease, assuming other factors remain constant
increase, assuming other factors remain constant
questions.explanation: The law of supply states a direct relationship between price and quantity supplied: higher prices generally motivate producers to supply more, ceteris paribus.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following is a major function of agricultural marketing?
options: Controlling the weather patterns affecting a farming season
Moving farm produce from the point of production to the final consumer efficiently
Increasing the biological yield of crops directly
Determining the genetic composition of livestock breeds
questions.explanation: Agricultural marketing covers all activities, assembling, storage, transport, processing, and distribution, that move produce from farm to consumer.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: An increase in the price of an agricultural commodity while all other factors remain constant is most likely to cause quantity demanded to
options: fall, in line with the law of demand
remain exactly the same at all price levels
rise sharply regardless of consumer income
become impossible to measure
questions.explanation: The law of demand states an inverse relationship between price and quantity demanded: as price rises, consumers generally buy less, other things being equal.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following is a major problem commonly associated with agricultural marketing in Nigeria?
options: An oversupply of cold storage facilities in every village
Poor rural road networks and inadequate storage facilities leading to high post-harvest losses
Too many well-organised marketing cooperatives nationwide
Excessive standardisation and grading of all produce
questions.explanation: Bad roads delay produce reaching markets while inadequate storage accelerates spoilage, together contributing significantly to post-harvest losses in Nigerian agriculture.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: The role of middlemen in agricultural marketing is best described as
options: growing crops on behalf of farmers
setting government agricultural policy
conducting agricultural research on new crop varieties
linking producers to final consumers by performing functions such as buying, transporting, and distributing produce
questions.explanation: Middlemen (assemblers, wholesalers, retailers) perform essential marketing functions that bridge the gap between scattered farm producers and dispersed consumers.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following best describes 'farm budgeting'?
options: A financial plan estimating expected income and expenditure of a farm business over a period
A map showing the boundaries of a farm
A list of all livestock breeds kept on a farm
A record of the weather conditions on a farm throughout the year
questions.explanation: Farm budgeting projects anticipated costs and revenues, helping a farmer plan resource allocation and assess likely profitability before committing to production.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a fixed cost in farm business management?
options: Depreciation on farm machinery
Wages paid to casual labourers hired for harvesting
Cost of seeds purchased for planting
Cost of fertiliser applied each season
questions.explanation: Fixed costs do not vary with the level of output in the short run; machinery depreciation is incurred regardless of how much is produced, unlike seed, fertiliser, or seasonal labour costs.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Farm profit is calculated as
options: total quantity produced multiplied by the number of farm workers
total revenue plus total cost of production
total cost of production divided by total revenue
total revenue minus total cost of production
questions.explanation: Profit is the surplus remaining after all production costs are subtracted from the total revenue generated from selling farm produce.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following best explains the term 'agricultural extension'?
options: A type of farm insurance policy
The physical enlargement of a farmer's landholding
An educational process of transferring useful research-based information to farmers to improve their practices
A government tax levied on farm produce
questions.explanation: Agricultural extension is fundamentally an informal education system that communicates research findings and improved techniques from scientists to farmers.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following is the most commonly used method by extension agents to reach many farmers at once with a new farming technique?
options: Individual farm visits to only one farmer per year
Restricting information strictly to university students
Method demonstration at farmer field days
Publishing research exclusively in international scientific journals
questions.explanation: Demonstrations at field days allow an extension agent to show a new technique practically to a large group of farmers simultaneously, encouraging wider adoption.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the role of the Agricultural Development Programme (ADP) in Nigeria?
options: Providing free land to every citizen who requests it
Setting the exchange rate of the Nigerian currency
Coordinating extension services and improved input distribution to boost farmer productivity at the state level
Manufacturing all fertiliser used in the country
questions.explanation: ADPs were established across Nigerian states primarily to deliver extension services, disseminate improved technology, and support farmers with access to inputs.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following is a key barrier to the adoption of improved agricultural technology by many rural farmers?
options: Limited access to credit and inadequate awareness of the new technology's benefits
Overexposure to too many extension agents per farmer
Complete absence of any traditional farming knowledge
Excessive availability of low-interest agricultural loans
questions.explanation: Farmers often cannot afford or are unaware of the advantages of new inputs or practices, which slows the adoption of otherwise beneficial agricultural innovations.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following best defines 'agricultural credit'?
options: A grading certificate issued for exported produce
Free farm inputs distributed without any repayment obligation
A government subsidy paid only to agricultural researchers
Funds borrowed by a farmer to finance farm operations, to be repaid usually with interest
questions.explanation: Agricultural credit refers to loans, obtained from banks, cooperatives, or other lenders, that farmers use to finance inputs, equipment, or expansion, and later repay.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following is a major benefit of forming a farmers' cooperative society for the marketing of produce?
options: Guaranteed freedom from any form of price fluctuation
Automatic elimination of all transportation costs
Increased bargaining power leading to better prices for members' produce
Removal of the need for any record-keeping
questions.explanation: By selling collectively, cooperative members can negotiate more favourable prices than they could individually, strengthening their position in the market.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: The concept of 'diminishing returns' in agricultural production describes a situation where
options: additional units of a variable input eventually produce smaller and smaller increases in output, other inputs held constant
adding any input always causes total output to fall immediately
output continues to increase at a constant rate no matter how much input is added
output rises only when land area is reduced
questions.explanation: The law of diminishing returns states that beyond a certain point, each extra unit of a variable input (e.g., fertiliser) yields progressively smaller output gains.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following farm records is used mainly to track the health treatments and productivity of individual livestock?
options: Farm map
Livestock/herd register
Soil survey report
Rainfall record
questions.explanation: A herd register logs details such as breed, health treatments, breeding history, and productivity for each animal, distinct from weather, mapping, or soil records.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following best describes 'value addition' in agricultural produce?
options: Processing raw farm produce into a more refined or convenient form to increase its market value
Reducing the quantity of produce available for sale
Selling raw produce immediately after harvest without any processing
Storing produce indefinitely without any further use
questions.explanation: Value addition, such as milling grain into flour or processing cassava into garri, increases a product's usefulness and market price compared with selling it raw.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following best explains why storage facilities are important in agricultural marketing?
options: They eliminate the need for transportation of produce to market
They permanently prevent any produce from ever being sold
They automatically increase the biological yield of the next planting season
They help reduce post-harvest losses and allow produce to be sold when prices are more favourable
questions.explanation: Proper storage protects harvested produce from spoilage and pests while giving farmers flexibility to sell later when market prices improve, rather than being forced to sell immediately.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following best describes 'land tenure' as it relates to agriculture?
options: The chemical composition of the topsoil on a farm
The system of rules and rights governing the ownership, holding, and use of land
The physical fertility level of a particular piece of farmland
The type of crop that must be grown on a piece of land by law
questions.explanation: Land tenure refers to the legal and customary arrangements determining who may own, inherit, lease, or use land, which strongly influences farming decisions and investment.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Communal land tenure, common in many traditional Nigerian communities, is best described as a system where
options: all farmland belongs exclusively to commercial banks
each individual holds a government-issued freehold title to their own separate plot
land is owned collectively by a community or family group and allocated to members for use
land can only be used by foreign investors
questions.explanation: Under communal tenure, land ownership rests with the community or extended family, with individual members granted use rights rather than full private ownership.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following best explains the economic principle of 'opportunity cost' as applied to a farmer's decision to plant maize instead of yam on a plot of land?
options: The value of the next best alternative (yam) that is forgone by choosing to plant maize
The amount of labour required to plant maize
The total cost of fertiliser used for the maize crop only
The market price of maize at harvest time
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the benefit of the best alternative given up when a choice is made; here, it is the value of the yam crop foregone by choosing to plant maize instead.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following best describes 'agricultural insurance'?
options: A tax imposed on farmers who fail to meet production quotas
A scheme that compensates farmers for losses arising from risks such as drought, flood, pests, or disease
A loan given only for the purchase of livestock feed
A savings account used exclusively for personal, non-farm expenses
questions.explanation: Agricultural insurance protects farmers financially against unpredictable losses from natural disasters, pests, or diseases in exchange for periodic premium payments.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Grading of agricultural produce before sale is important mainly because it
options: classifies produce by quality, allowing fairer pricing and easier marketing
increases the biological growth rate of the crop after harvest
reduces the nutritional value of the produce
eliminates the need for any form of packaging
questions.explanation: Grading sorts produce into quality categories (e.g., by size or ripeness), enabling buyers to pay appropriate prices and simplifying transactions in the market.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following best illustrates 'specialisation' in agricultural production?
options: A farmer who changes their main enterprise every single week
A farmer who refuses to sell any of their produce
A farmer who focuses exclusively on poultry production rather than growing many different crops and animals
A farmer who grows ten different crops and keeps five different livestock species on the same small plot
questions.explanation: Specialisation involves concentrating resources and effort on one enterprise (e.g., poultry) to gain efficiency and expertise, rather than spreading effort across many unrelated enterprises.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the function of the Nigerian Commodity Exchange in agricultural marketing?
options: Providing an organised platform for the trading of standardised agricultural commodities
Setting the biological maturity period of every crop
Replacing the need for farmers to harvest their own produce
Directly cultivating crops on behalf of the government
questions.explanation: A commodity exchange creates a formal, regulated marketplace where standardised, graded agricultural products can be traded transparently between buyers and sellers.
